plan.coverage_explanation: Checks suppression outside 20 cm at both ADC endpoints, then requires alarm reporting and LED/buzzer activity over a combined near-object interval containing both endpoints. The combined interval does not assign a darkness polarity or threshold: either endpoint may produce the required activity. This rejects a no-output implementation. Coverage remains partial because the unspecified light classification and timing prevent independent assertions of the light gate, exact distance boundary, blink cadence, and intermittent buzzer pauses.
assumptions: Relies on the bench default that the D13 LED is active HIGH; A0 uses raw ADC values.

The light-divider polarity and darkness threshold are unspecified. The endpoint exercise assumes a meaningful light-sensitive classification: the full ADC range includes a dark condition, with at least one endpoint classified dark. No particular endpoint or intermediate threshold is required.
D6 is a passive tone output, consistent with the authoritative tone_output role.

Six seconds at each near-object endpoint allows practical sensor acquisition and observable alarm activity. No precise sampling interval, blink period, tone frequency, or reporting repetition rate is required.
No alarm-cancellation deadline is imposed: all outside-range checks precede potentially alarming inputs.
The reference chooses ADC below 500 as dark, 70 ms sampling, 250 ms alarm phases, and a 2000 Hz tone. These are implementation choices, not candidate expectations.
Serial alarm reporting may occur only on entry; the positive reporting window includes both near-object endpoint states.
